Subject: Distributor credit mapping + volume trigger alignment for Azure PO

Marcus —

Thanks for the time on Friday. We’re finalizing the economics for the Azure private offer and a couple of open items came up on our side that we need to lock before procurement signs:

- How do you prefer we structure distributor credits for a reseller that invoices monthly but reconciles quarterly?
- Can volume-triggered credits be issued retroactively on settled invoices, or do you need an upfront holdback / escrow arrangement?
- What evidence will Redwood accept from the distributor to validate pass-through credits (invoice PDFs, GL extracts, signed distributor confirmation)?

I’m copying our distributor ops team (dist-ops) — they’ll provide sample invoice cadence.

Attachments: Distributor_Evidence.zip (sample invoices), NexHealth-SOW-v3.pdf

Appreciate a short note on the preferred path (monthly pass-through vs quarterly holdback) and any templated evidence Redwood needs.

Best,
Laura
Head of Procurement
NexHealth Systems
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Mendes <laura.m@nexthealthsys.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Distributor Team <dist-ops@nexhealthsys.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Distributor credit mapping + volume trigger alignment for Azure PO

Laura — thanks, this is helpful. Quick summary of our recommended approach and questions for the distributor ops team: 

1) Primary option (preferred): monthly pass-through with monthly supporting artifacts.
   - When the reseller invoices monthly but reconciles quarterly, Redwood can accept a monthly pass-through payment to the reseller if the reseller provides: invoice PDF, invoice line showing Redwood-listed SKU, and a distributor confirmation statement for the month.
   - Quarterly reconciliation: if the distributor performs a quarterly true-up, Redwood will accommodate a one-time retrospective adjustment to the customer invoice via a credit note, provided the monthly artifacts were submitted for each month in the quarter.

2) Alternate (holdback): quarterly holdback/escrow that releases after distributor evidence is validated. Use only if the distributor cannot produce monthly artifacts.

3) Evidence types accepted: invoice PDFs, distributor GL export (CSV), signed distributor confirmation (simple template). We prefer structured CSV mappings for automated reconciliation. I’m attaching an example mapping (example_credit_mapping.csv) and the Azure PO template (azure_po_template.pdf) showing where credits are documented in the offer.

Actions / asks for dist-ops:
- Can you confirm invoice cadence and whether you can export a per-month GL for the quarter?
- If you can’t do monthly artifacts, we’ll move to the holdback route and outline the release conditions.

Next steps: once dist-ops confirms cadence, Redwood sales ops will add language to the PO about "credit pass-through" and include required evidence fields. After that we’ll update the HubSpot deal and prepare the DocuSign packet.

If helpful I can propose a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Market & Channel GTM
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Laura —

Quick answers from distributor ops: we invoice monthly (day 5 of the following month) and do a full GL reconciliation on the 1st business day after quarter close. We can export per-month GL extracts, but it requires a little transformation (we can provide CSV; see Distributor_Evidence.zip).

Two notes:
- The reseller asks that any retrospective credits be applied as a single quarterly credit rather than three separate monthly credits (one credit per month) for bookkeeping simplicity. Is that acceptable to Redwood?
- For the volume-triggered retro credit: we can sign a short confirmation form if Redwood needs an extra attestation step (signed by dist-ops).

We prefer the quarterly true-up (single credit) if Redwood can accept a quarterly credit note based on month-by-month artifacts aggregated at quarter-end.

Thanks,
Amit Rao
Head of Distributor Ops
NexHealth Distribution

Subject: Re: Distributor credit mapping + volume trigger alignment for Azure PO

Thanks Amit — that cadence works and the single quarterly credit is an acceptable operational compromise. Recap and final path: 

- Redwood will accept a single quarterly credit note applied to the reseller’s account provided: (a) monthly artifacts (invoice PDFs + GL CSV) are supplied for each month in the quarter, and (b) a signed distributor confirmation form is supplied at quarter close.
- Redwood will emit the quarterly credit within 30 days of receipt of complete artifacts and signed confirmation.
- If monthly artifacts are not provided for any month, Redwood will require a holdback for that month equal to the projected credit until evidence is provided.

Open items I’ll action this week: 
- Vanessa will draft the short distributor confirmation template and share it with Amit by EOD Friday.
